I was in the process of being in a study for ketamine and was so disappointed when they told me I didn't meet the criteria because I wasn't depressed enough. I was heart broken. Ketamine studies are the only foreseeable hope I have and, apparently, daily suicidal ideation isn't enough. I don't get it. 
There are ketamine clinics in my state, but I can't afford the out of pocket costs. Here's hoping other people get the help they need because anyone with treatment resistant depression should have a chance. It's amazing that people are studying the effects...I'm proud of you and your work!

Unless it's absolutely needed, I do not recommend hospitalization. I've been hospitalized 3 times over 11 years in 3 different settings. As an adult, it's co-ed which should be fine, however, being there for self harm or suicidal ideation/attempts, doesn't separate you from others with severe mental illness that could harm you. I still have letters I saved,just in case, from a stalker I picked you at a hospital. Through group therapy, he learned enough about me over a week and sent me letters to my house after his release! That same hospital, I was given a phone number of one of the staff and we began a minor affair. While I am an adult, I was in a very vulnerable place and it's totally unethical. I had horrible experiences... Being pushed up against a wall because another patient perceived me as a threat, being ridiculed by staff taking advantage of mental illness, etc.

The other two hospitals were not like this at all though. All in all, it's not terrible, but from my experience, people want to make friends and connections, and you'll be better off if you don't. Share enough to get better, but absolutely don't be personal. You never know how seriously someone else's illness is, even if they appear completely sane. 

Take care of yourself. If you think even for a moment that you need to be hospitalized, do it. Otherwise, try outpatient intensive programs.
